clue.text: Lucky animal avoiding pound, biting horse's lip

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so the abbreviation for pound is left out
whatever bites closes its jaws around something, so the shortened animal wraps round the horse

blocks.note: a black cat is a traditional British good-luck symbol
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling (libra)
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A lucky black cat nips a horse on the lip.
explanation.walkthrough: BLACK CAT loses its L to become BACKCAT, which then closes round H to give BACKCHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip is informal for cheeky, impudent talk, the same thing as answering back rudely.

clue.text: Robbers' song heard when propping up bar

definitions.note: the clue's possessive is surface only; the answer is a plural noun

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for song counts by its sound alone

blocks.note: to bar is to prohibit, to ban
a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: Bandits sing a song while leaning on a pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the piece propping up another sits below it, so the song follows BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is the Italian plural of bandit, used in English for outlaw gangs who rob travellers.

clue.text: Heavenly body yours truly enticed into bed?

indicators.note: someone enticed into a place is drawn inside it, so the setter's pronoun goes within the bed

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
yours truly is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A gorgeous person lures the speaker to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavenly body suggests a beautiful figure, but it is an astronomical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy celestial object orbiting the sun, trailing a glowing tail across the sky.

clue.text: Fail finally to get money for potatoes?

blocks.note: first meaning: to die, an idiom from the gambling table
second meaning, read literally: to exchange fried potato chips for money

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from gamblers handing in their gaming chips at the end of play; British chips are also fried potato strips.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a euphemism for dying, and literally describes turning chips into cash.

clue.text: Unsurpassed army officer hiding in a tree

indicators.note: someone hiding in a place is concealed inside it, so the officer sits within the tree

blocks.note: taken as written
the lime, or linden, is a tree
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A record-breaking army officer hides up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record or best has never been beaten, so it is unequalled ever.

clue.text: Beetle found in tar by craggy outcrop

blocks.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff or outcrop
a tar is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)

explanation.surface: A beetle turns up in tar beside a rocky crag.
explanation.walkthrough: Tar looks like the sticky black stuff, but in crosswords it is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Commit oneself to scrub her coins for distribution

indicators.note: things set out for distribution are spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone commits to cleaning her coins before handing them out.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar crossing the river Rubicon in 49 BC committed him to civil war, with no way back.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take an irrevocable step, pledging oneself to a course of action.

clue.text: What the board did — turned out sour and bitter

indicators.note: turned out means rearranged or overturned, so the letters of that word are reordered

blocks.note: a board of directors ran the company: RAN plus CO for company
taken as written, to be reordered

explanation.surface: The board's decision left everyone sour and bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a company board of directors, whose job is to run the company, abbreviated CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous means full of long-held resentment and spite, so bitter in feeling.

clue.text: Oppressive duty, forming chorus

blocks.note: first meaning: a heavy load of responsibility
second meaning: the refrain of a song, an older sense of the word

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is less familiar: it is the repeated refrain of a song or poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a heavy load or obligation and the recurring refrain of a song.

clue.text: Messengers a German Marxist beheaded

indicators.note: beheading removes the head, so the first letter of the Marxist's name is lost

blocks.note: taken as written
Friedrich Engels, Marx's German collaborator

explanation.surface: Messengers report that a German communist has been executed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek angelos means messenger; angels deliver divine messages in scripture.

clue.text: New house backing site of Roman remains in France

definitions.text: site of Roman remains in France

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for this kind of house is written right to left

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
a semi is a semi-detached house, one sharing a wall with its neighbour

explanation.surface: A newly built house seems to back on to Roman ruins in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Nîmes in southern France keeps a famous Roman arena and the Maison Carrée temple.

clue.text: Squire taking narrow road right across hill

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching over it on both sides, so the road and its partner enclose the hill

blocks.note: a lane is a narrow country road
R is the abbreviation for right
a down is a rolling chalk hill, as in the South Downs

explanation.surface: A country squire takes a narrow lane over the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The hill goes inside LANE, before its last letter, and R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A squire was the chief owner of land in an English village, so a property holder of estates.

clue.text: Untaught Alaskan native the writer's taken on? About time

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the native people go round the abbreviation for time

blocks.note: the Inuit are an indigenous Arctic people, including in Alaska
T is the abbreviation for time
the writer is the setter, I, and 's here stands for has: I've

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an untaught Alaskan native has been hired by the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is the setter, and the writer's here means 'I have', contracted; the question mark flags that odd reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuitive knowledge comes by instinct rather than instruction, so it is untaught.

clue.text: Product of baker in ancient Scottish settlement

blocks.note: first meaning: a small round baked cake eaten with butter or jam
second meaning: the old Perthshire village where Scottish kings were crowned

explanation.surface: A baker's wares are found in an old Scottish village.
explanation.walkthrough: Scone in Perthshire gave its name to the Stone of Scone, the coronation stone of Scottish kings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small baked teatime cake and the historic Scottish royal site.

clue.text: He leaves the work complete, say? Excellent

indicators.note: when he leaves he departs, so those two letters go from the phrase for the work
say asks us to speak the word for complete, keeping its sound but not its spelling

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
taken as written, to be removed
whole means complete, and sounds like a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: A man walks off, leaving his work all finished — excellent!
explanation.walkthrough: THE OP without H and E leaves TOP; WHOLE spoken aloud gives HOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-hole is dated upper-class British slang meaning first-rate or splendid.

clue.text: Pressure afflicted priest in such a suit

indicators.note: something afflicted is troubled and out of sorts, so these letters are upset into a new order

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure
taken as written, to be reordered

explanation.surface: A troubled priest is under pressure while wearing a smart suit.
explanation.walkthrough: In looks like a link to the suit but is part of the letters to reorder.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinstripe is a business suit of cloth with fine vertical lines, the kind referred to.

clue.text: Train from Soho travelling round west end of Central Line

indicators.note: things travelling are moving about, so these letters move into a new order
on a map west is the left, and the left end of a written word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written: the London district
the first letter of this word
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A train sets off from Soho on the London Underground's Central Line.
explanation.walkthrough: Train looks like a noun on the Tube; it is the verb. Soho is a London district and the Central Line an Underground route.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or drill them, just as to train them.

clue.text: In the morning, ride around northern plant

indicators.note: the word for ride goes around the abbreviation for morning, enclosing it

blocks.note: to cycle is to ride a bike
am is ante meridiem, before noon
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Someone cycles around a northern plant early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The cyclamen is a flowering plant with swept-back petals, popular in pots.

clue.text: Small picture capturing start of county cricket?

indicators.note: to capture is to take and hold inside, so the small picture closes round a letter
the start of a word is its first letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: an inset is a small picture set within a larger one
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A small photograph captures the opening of a county cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: County cricket is the English domestic game, but the question mark warns that cricket here is the chirping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is a chirping, jumping creature, one example of a six-legged invertebrate.

clue.text: Chuckle when non-drinker gets involved in row

indicators.note: getting involved in something means getting inside it, so the abstainer is put within the row

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
TT is teetotal, a person abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: People laugh when the teetotaller gets into an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Row suggests a quarrel, but it is a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A titter is a short, half-suppressed laugh, much like a quiet giggle.

clue.text: Uncivil servant initially rejected the old form of obeisance

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of the word just before it
something rejected is sent back, so the old word for the is written backwards

blocks.note: curt means rudely brief
the first letter of this word
ye is the old written form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

explanation.surface: A rude servant refuses the old-fashioned bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsey is a woman's respectful bob or bend of the knee, a gesture of deference.

clue.text: Conservative heavyweight axing British warship

indicators.note: to axe is to cut out, so the abbreviation for British is chopped from the heavyweight

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a bruiser is a big, tough fighter
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A Tory political heavyweight scraps a British warship.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavyweight suggests a senior politician, but here it is a burly fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiser is a fast, well-armed naval vessel, one class of fighting ship.

clue.text: Finally heeding publicity, purchase useful device

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the last letter of this word
an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
to get is to obtain or buy

explanation.surface: Someone, swayed at last by advertising, buys a handy device.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small mechanical tool or contrivance designed for a practical job.

clue.text: Language once used by investigator pursuing extremists

blocks.note: A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: Some old tongue was spoken by a detective tailing radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: Extremists suggests fanatics; here it means the two letters at either end of the alphabet, which the detective follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Aztec, or Nahuatl, was the tongue spoken in the Mexican empire before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Sort of sketch that pins Tom down?

blocks.note: surface reading: a kind of small, quick drawing
setter's reading: a spike that would pin the tiny fairy-tale hero Tom to the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of an English folk tale, so a nail sized to pin him down would be a very small one.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail sketch is a brief, small-scale drawing or outline, no bigger than the nail on your thumb.

clue.text: Assemble article in a number of handwritten sheets

indicators.note: in places the article inside the abbreviation for the handwritten sheets

blocks.note: taken as written
MSS is the abbreviation for manuscripts
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone gathers an article together from a pile of handwritten pages.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate a large quantity, so to collect together.

clue.text: Stern head transfixed by one's filthy state

indicators.note: transfixed means pierced right through, so the numeral one is stuck into the middle

blocks.note: grim means severe and stern
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours or Sheerness
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A stern headmaster, pinned by someone's gaze, is in a filthy state.
explanation.walkthrough: GRIM and NESS sit side by side and the I spears the join between them; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Griminess is the condition of being covered in ingrained dirt, so a filthy state.

clue.text: Spell "desirability"

blocks.note: first meaning: a magic incantation
second meaning: the quality of being attractive and appealing

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks us to spell out a word; spell is a noun meaning an enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a magical incantation and an attractive, appealing quality in a person.

clue.text: Very small place for driving school's opening in city

indicators.note: an opening is the very beginning, so only the first letter of that word counts
in places that letter inside the abbreviation for the city

blocks.note: a golfer drives off from the tee
NY is New York
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A tiny parking spot is available for a driving school opening in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Driving suggests cars and a driving school, but it is a golf drive, taken from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Teensy is an informal, childlike word for tiny, minute or very little.

clue.text: Relative sum of money laid out by star on radio.

indicators.note: on radio we only hear words, so the star is taken by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars
the Sun is our star, and its name is pronounced like a male child

explanation.surface: A relative pays out a big sum to a radio celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Star suggests a radio celebrity; it is the Sun, heard as SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson is the son of one's child, a family member and so a relative.
